introduction: I use lipid biomarkers to reconstruct past climates, ecosystems, and human impacts from lake sediments. My work combines molecular distributions and compound-specific δ²H and δ¹³C measurements with other evidence preserved in these natural archives.
context: Interpreting these records requires understanding both environmental conditions and the organisms that produce the molecules we measure. I combine modern calibration studies with sedimentary records to investigate source effects, refine biomarker proxies, and make the uncertainties in past environmental reconstructions explicit.

projects.title: MEMELAND
projects.summary: Reconstructing medieval land use from lake sediments, using fecal and plant biomarkers to trace farming practices and environmental impacts.
projects.question: How can molecular traces in lake sediments reveal medieval farming practices and their environmental impacts?
projects.about:
MEMELAND is an ERC Synergy project funded under the European Union’s Horizon Europe programme. It began on 1 July 2025 and investigates how human land use has shaped European landscapes and biodiversity over the last two millennia. It combines lake-sediment archives with archaeological, palaeoecological, and molecular evidence to distinguish local land-use histories from regional change.

Read more about [the Eawag team’s research](https://memeland.no/en/Team/eawag.html).
projects.approach:
- **Grazing and manuring:** Fecal sterols and bile acids will trace animal and human inputs, complement animal sedimentary DNA records, and test links between nutrient enrichment and low-oxygen lake conditions.
- **Soil erosion:** Compound-specific radiocarbon dating of leaf waxes and refractory organic carbon analyses will investigate soil disturbance linked to ploughing and livestock.
- **Crop cultivation:** Miliacin (millet) and cannabinol (*Cannabis* spp.) will be used to investigate cultivation and practices such as hemp retting.

Biomarker records will be integrated with hyperspectral imaging and geochemical and chronological data from the University of Salzburg team. Together with archaeobotany, sedimentary DNA, and socio-environmental modelling, these records will help compare medieval agricultural practices across Europe.
projects.contribution: I will join Prof. [Nathalie Dubois](https://memeland.no/en/Team/people.html#prof.-dr.-nathalie-dubois) in the Eawag team’s biomarker work, using lake sediments to reconstruct medieval agricultural practices and their effects on aquatic ecosystems.

projects.title: ADAPT
projects.summary: Using lipid biomarkers and sedimentary DNA to understand how lake algal communities respond to natural change and human activity.
projects.question: How can we distinguish hydroclimate signals from changes in terrestrial and aquatic plant sources in sedimentary lipid records?
projects.about:
ADAPT (Algal Dynamics and Productivity through Time) is a Swiss National Science Foundation project investigating how lake algal communities respond to natural environmental change and human activity. It combines lipid biomarkers and sedimentary DNA to reconstruct past algal communities and their links to water quality, food webs, and carbon cycling.

My PhD contribution connects modern calibration studies in northeastern Germany with lake-sediment archives from Switzerland and northeastern North America. It develops ways to account for lipid source changes and reconstruct the climatic context of past ecosystem change.

ADAPT is funded through an SNSF Eccellenza Professorial Fellowship awarded to S. Nemiah Ladd.
projects.approach:
- **Modern calibration:** Compare lipid biomarkers and sedimentary DNA in water and surface sediments with living algal communities, and characterise lipid distributions and hydrogen-isotope fractionation in charophytes and submerged vascular plants.
- **Vegetation-corrected hydroclimate:** Use the relative abundances of long-chain n-alkanes to account for vegetation effects in plant-wax δ²H records from Rotsee and Owasco, and interpret climate change since the last deglaciation alongside other sedimentary evidence.
- **Past algal dynamics:** Investigate how nutrient enrichment, changes in water quality, and natural environmental variability have shaped algal communities throughout the Holocene. Swiss-lake studies address 20th-century phosphorus changes and Roman-period water-quality impacts. Comparable assessments of algal dynamics also include Owasco and Skaneateles lakes in New York, USA.
- **Aquatic sources and vegetation:** Combine lipid distributions, compound-specific δ²H and δ¹³C measurements, and modern calibration data to interpret aquatic biomarker indices and reconstruct changes in macroalgal abundance.
projects.contribution:
My contribution focuses on distinguishing hydroclimate signals from changes in the plants that supply lipids to lake sediments. I combine modern aquatic-plant calibration in northeastern Germany with vegetation-corrected plant-wax δ²H records from Lake Rotsee in Switzerland and Owasco Lake in New York.

This work tests how source changes affect aquatic biomarker indices and reduces vegetation-related shifts in sedimentary isotope records, helping reconstruct past hydroclimate and provide context for changes in lake ecosystems.
projects.overview_text:
This work formed part of my PhD in the Organic Geochemistry group at the University of Basel, supervised by Prof. Nemiah Ladd. I investigated how changes in lipid sources affect sedimentary records from temperate lakes in Europe and northeastern North America, and how these effects can be identified, quantified, and corrected.

Plant-derived lipids, including long-chain n-alkanes, fatty acids, and phytol, preserve evidence of past climate and vegetation. Their hydrogen-isotope values (δ²H) are particularly useful for reconstructing hydroclimate. Yet lipids reach sediments from both the lake and its catchment: shifts between aquatic and terrestrial plants, or between grasses and trees, can alter the isotope signal even when precipitation remains unchanged.

I combined modern calibration data with sediment records extending back to the last deglaciation. In northeastern Germany, I showed that charophytes and submerged vascular plants differ in their lipid production and hydrogen-isotope fractionation, with implications for how widely used aquatic biomarker indices are interpreted.

At Lake Rotsee in Switzerland and Owasco Lake in New York, I tested and applied a vegetation correction based on the relative abundances of long-chain n-alkanes. Accounting for vegetation effects substantially reduced abrupt late-Holocene isotope shifts associated with forest clearance and agricultural expansion. The corrected records reveal clearer, regionally coherent hydroclimate signals linked to insolation, ice-sheet retreat, and atmospheric circulation. Together, these results highlight the importance of accounting for source changes when interpreting sedimentary lipid δ²H.

projects.title: HOLMODRIVE · Lake Peixão
projects.summary: Reading the Lake Peixão sediment archive to understand climate, vegetation, and environmental change in western Iberia.
projects.question: How have North Atlantic climate variability, vegetation, and human activity shaped the environment around Lake Peixão?
projects.about: HOLMODRIVE (*North Atlantic Atmospheric Patterns Influence on Western Iberia Climate: From the Late Glacial to the Present*) explored the links between large-scale atmospheric circulation and environmental change in western Iberia. At Lake Peixão in Portugal’s Serra da Estrela, the sediment archive records changes in climate, vegetation, and the surrounding landscape.
projects.approach: A multi-proxy approach combining lipid biomarkers and compound-specific stable isotope measurements (δ²H and δ¹³C) with pollen, diatoms, chironomids, macrocharcoal, sedimentology, and inorganic geochemistry. Together, these complementary records help reconstruct past hydroclimate, vegetation, lake ecology, and landscape change.
projects.contribution:
I began by characterising the leaf-wax n-alkane distributions and isotopic signatures of dominant plants, soil, and surface sediment around the lake. This calibration identified the δ²H of the C₂₉ n-alkane as a robust indicator of terrestrial hydrology in Lake Peixão sediments and established a baseline for interpreting leaf-wax records in western Iberia.

I then applied these proxies downcore to reconstruct vegetation and hydroclimate over the last 2,000 years. The record documents shifts in Atlantic and Mediterranean climate influences through the Medieval Climate Anomaly and the Little Ice Age, linking vegetation change to large-scale atmospheric dynamics.

I also contributed to multi-proxy studies of the core’s chronology, deglaciation, and Saharan dust and sea-salt inputs since the Late Glacial.

projects.overview_text:
During my time at IPMA and the University of Lisbon, I worked on Lake Peixão, a small glacial lake at around 1,700 m in Serra da Estrela. Its position between Atlantic and Mediterranean climate influences makes its sediments a sensitive archive of environmental change in western Iberia.

I led the organic geochemistry work on the PEX19-01 sediment core, analysing leaf-wax n-alkanes and their compound-specific δ²H and δ¹³C values.
